hints: Apply the given fixed-point formula repeatedly, carrying each displayed iterate to 6 decimal places.
Start with $x_1=2$ and substitute each result back as the next input.
Continue until successive 6-decimal iterates agree sufficiently to determine the same value to 4 decimal places.
walkthrough:
Notice that $x_4$ and $x_5$ both round to $1.319508$ to 6 decimal places.
Round the converged value to 4 decimal places:
$$\alpha \approx 1.3195$$

hints: At the limit of a convergent iteration, consecutive terms have the same value $\alpha$.
Use $\alpha>0$ from the iteration to simplify the resulting polynomial condition and express the root exactly.
walkthrough:
Since the sequence converges to $\alpha$, the limit satisfies $x_{n+1} = x_n = \alpha$:
$$\alpha = \dfrac{2\alpha^6 + 12\alpha}{3\alpha^5 + 8}$$

Multiply both sides by the denominator $(3\alpha^5 + 8)$:
$$\alpha(3\alpha^5 + 8) = 2\alpha^6 + 12\alpha$$
$$3\alpha^6 + 8\alpha = 2\alpha^6 + 12\alpha$$

Collect all terms on the left-hand side:
$$3\alpha^6 - 2\alpha^6 + 8\alpha - 12\alpha = 0$$
$$\alpha^6 - 4\alpha = 0$$

Take the fifth root of both sides to obtain the exact value of $\alpha$:
$$\alpha = \sqrt[5]{4} \quad \left(\text{or } 4^{\frac{1}{5}} = 2^{\frac{2}{5}}\right)$$
